title: Stones Taro's 'Physics': Kyoto's Maestro Redefines the UK Underground
summary: Japanese artist Stones Taro is set to drop his highly anticipated new EP, 'Physics,' on September 18, 2026, through Faux Poly. The Kyoto-based producer continues to push sonic boundaries, masterfully blending UKG and house to deliver a truly fresh sound to the global dance scene.
content:
From the vibrant streets of Kyoto, Japan, a unique sonic architect is once again set to turn heads in the global electronic music scene. Stones Taro, a name already synonymous with innovative soundscapes, is gearing up to release his latest EP, 'Physics,' on September 18, 2026, via the esteemed Faux Poly label.

Despite his Japanese origins, Taro is undeniably a spiritual successor to the UK underground. His musical DNA is deeply steeped in the rhythms and sensibilities of British dance music, a passion he expertly transmutes into something entirely his own. Fans and critics alike have long celebrated his knack for crafting what can only be described as 'carbonated cocktails' – an effervescent blend of UK Garage (UKG) and house music that is both familiar and refreshingly new. His previous releases on influential labels like Rhythm Section have solidified his reputation as a producer unafraid to explore the interstitial spaces between genres.

'Physics' promises to be no exception, reportedly breaking new ground even for an artist known for his forward-thinking approach. Expect intricate drum patterns, deep, resonant basslines, and euphoric synth melodies that build and release tension with masterful precision. It's a testament to his artistry that he can take established genres and infuse them with such an individualistic energy, creating tracks that feel timeless yet utterly contemporary. Stones Taro isn't just making music; he's crafting an auditory experience that transcends geographical boundaries, proving that the heart of the underground beats globally.
keyTakeaways: Stones Taro, hailing from Kyoto, is heavily influenced by the UK underground scene, blending UKG and house music.
His new EP, 'Physics,' is set for release on September 18, 2026, through the Faux Poly label.
The EP is anticipated to further solidify his reputation for genre-bending innovation and refreshing soundscapes.
author: Henry Ivry

title: Musk's Grok Turns to Digital Graveyard for Data Gold
summary: Elon Musk's xAI, behind the Grok chatbot, is reportedly looking beyond X and SpaceX data to acquire vast datasets from defunct startups. This unconventional strategy highlights the intense global demand for training data in the race for advanced AI, sparking questions about data ethics and privacy.
content:
In the relentless pursuit of artificial general intelligence (AGI), data reigns supreme, and its acquisition often dictates the pace of innovation. For Elon Musk’s burgeoning xAI, the company behind the Grok chatbot, it seems even the sprawling archives of X (formerly Twitter) and the technical telemetry from SpaceX aren’t quite enough to satiate its voracious appetite.

Reports suggest that Grok's journey toward more sophisticated capabilities requires a far broader and deeper dataset than what can be gleaned from social media chatter or rocket launches. This isn't merely about volume; it's about the sheer diversity and specialized nature of information needed to train a truly advanced model capable of nuanced understanding and reasoning across myriad domains.

This insatiable demand has reportedly led xAI down an unconventional path: exploring the acquisition of customer data from defunct startups. In a world where premium datasets command exorbitant prices, the digital graveyards of failed ventures represent a tantalizing, potentially cheaper, and often untapped reservoir of information. These could include anything from user interactions with niche apps to proprietary business intelligence accumulated before their demise.

While resourceful, such a strategy isn't without its complexities. Legal frameworks around data ownership, privacy, and user consent for data collected by a now-defunct entity are murky, to say the least. Quality control also poses a significant hurdle; sifting through and sanitizing data from multiple disparate sources requires immense effort. Yet, this aggressive hunt underscores the escalating data arms race among AI giants, illustrating the extraordinary lengths companies are willing to go to secure the foundational fuel for their generative models.

Musk’s latest reported gambit highlights a critical bottleneck in the AI revolution. As the quest for AGI intensifies, the true innovators might not just be those with the best algorithms, but those with the most ingenious – and perhaps audacious – strategies for feeding them the data they crave.
keyTakeaways: Elon Musk's xAI (Grok) is reportedly seeking customer data from defunct startups to bolster its AI training.
The move indicates that current data sources from X and SpaceX are insufficient for Grok's advanced AI ambitions.
This unconventional data acquisition strategy highlights the intense, expensive global race for diverse AI training data, raising significant legal and ethical questions.
author: Ece Yildirim
